$comment: Failure shapes for org.gleif.vlei/identity. Two of them, and the difference matters:
a missing capability is a configuration problem reported as a JSON-RPC error, while a
rejected credential is a tool result. Collapsing them tells the caller to fix the wrong thing.
Every rejection names its layer, because the correct recovery differs per layer and an agent
that receives only 'access denied' cannot choose one.
The server requires the extension; the client never declared it at initialize. Nothing was
verified and nothing was rejected — the conversation could not begin on these terms.
Note what this is not: it is not a refusal of a credential, and telling the user their
credential was refused would send them to the wrong place entirely.

error.message: server requires capabilities not declared by the client: org.gleif.vlei/identity

$comment: The extension was declared, a credential was presented, and a named check stopped the call.
The layer appears first and unadorned in the text so a model can key off it without
heuristics, and again in _meta for anything that parses rather than reads.

content.text: revoked: the credential has been revoked in the issuer's transaction event log

org.gleif.vlei/failure.message: the credential has been revoked in the issuer's transaction event log

layers.when: The tool declares a requirement and the caller presented no credential, or no signature.
layers.retry: No. Attach a credential. This is not a failure to verify — it is a failure to present, and keeping it separate sends the caller to the right fix.
layers.text: missing_credential: this tool requires an ECR credential and a signed request; the caller presented no credential

layers.when: The signature's timestamp is outside the freshness window, or the same (aid, digest, ts) was seen before.
layers.retry: Yes, once. If it fails again the clocks disagree by more than the window; say so rather than retrying further. This is the only retryable layer.
layers.text: stale_signature: signature timestamp is 312s from now, outside the 60s freshness window

layers.when: The received parameters do not hash to the digest that was signed — the request was altered after signing.
layers.retry: No. This is an integrity problem, not a transient one. Reported separately from invalid_signature because tampering in transit and a bad key state call for different responses.
layers.text: digest_mismatch: request arguments do not match the signed digest; they were altered after signing

layers.when: The signature does not verify under the presented AID's current key state.
layers.retry: No. Either the wrong key signed, or the key state has moved on. Both are configuration.
layers.text: invalid_signature: signature does not verify under the presented key state

layers.when: A SAID does not recompute, an edge points at a credential that was not presented, a link's issuer is not the previous link's issuee, or a revocation source could not be read at all.
layers.retry: No. Report it as a credential-configuration problem. Note the last case: an unreadable log is a failure to establish revocation, never an absence of it.
layers.text: chain_invalid: credential EM3weU… does not hash to its own SAID; its contents were altered

layers.when: A credential in the chain has been withdrawn in its issuer's transaction event log.
layers.retry: No, and not with a different credential either. The entity withdrew this authority; a new credential must be issued.
layers.text: revoked: the credential has been revoked in the issuer's transaction event log

layers.when: The chain is internally sound but terminates at a root the relying party does not accept.
layers.retry: No. Nothing is wrong with the credential and nothing is wrong with the server: two organizations disagree about whom they trust, and only they can resolve it. Report which root you chain to.
layers.text: unknown_root: chain terminates at EOther…, which is not an accepted root

layers.when: The presented ECR role does not satisfy the role the tool declared.
layers.retry: No. Name the required role and the one held; a new ECR must be issued by the legal entity.
layers.text: role_mismatch: tool requires role 'regulatory-filing'; the presented credential carries 'member-registration'

layers.when: The request falls outside the scope the tool declared, measured against the scope the credential carries.
layers.retry: Not as sent. A retry within the limit may be appropriate — ask the user first, and state the limit and the requested value.
layers.text: scope_exceeded: maxAmount: requires at least 1000000, credential carries 500000
